etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English compilen, from Old French compiler, from Latin compīlō (“to plunder”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To make by gathering pieces from various sources.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book III, Canto III”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: Before that Merlin dyde, he did intend / A brasen wall in compas to compyle / About Cairmardin  […]

definitions.definition: (transitive, snooker) To achieve (a break) by making a sequence of shots.
(transitive, programming) To use a compiler to process source code and produce executable code.
(intransitive, programming) To be successfully processed by a compiler into executable code.

quote.citation: 1595, Edmunde Spenser [i.e., Edmund Spenser], “[Amoretti.] Sonnet LXXX”, in Amoretti and Epithalamion. […], London:  […]  [Peter Short] for William Ponsonby, →OCLC, signature F, verso:
quote.text: After ſo long a race as I haue run / Through Faery land, vvhich theſe ſix books cõpile [compile], / giue leaue to reſt me being halfe fordonne, / and gather to my ſelfe nevv breath avvhile.

quote.citation: 1690, William Temple, Miscellanea. The Second Part. […], London:  […]  T. M. for Ri[chard] and Ra[lph] Simpson, […], →OCLC, section II, page 188:
quote.text: They are at their leisure much given to poetry; in which they compile the praises of virtuous men and actions , satires against vice

quote.citation: 1985, Robert A Stern, An Introduction to Computers and Information Processing:
quote.text: […]  programming team managers assumed the "improved programs" produced through structured programming would not require as many compiles during development.

quote.citation: 2007, Scott Meyers, Mike Lee, MAC OS X Leopard: Beyond the Manual:
quote.text: Any file with an error or warning on it will be added to this smart group until the next compile.
